title: Low-Complexity Algorithmic Test Generation for Neuromorphic Chips
problem: Neuromorphic chips lack design for testability (DfT) despite having many potential configurations, making comprehensive fault testing difficult. Efficient test generation methods that scale to large networks are needed.
motivation: Neuromorphic chips offer low-power AI acceleration, but effective testing methodologies are essential to ensure reliability and fault-free deployment.
method: The method systematically tests neuromorphic chips by creating test inputs that activate faults—making defective neurons behave differently from working ones. These faulty signals then propagate through the network layers, amplifying their effects so they can be detected at the network's output. For spiking neural networks with L layers, this approach achieves complete fault detection (100% coverage) using only L test configurations (meaning the number of tests scales linearly with network depth), while requiring minimal weight changes and tolerating 4-bit quantization (reduced numerical precision).
key_novelty: A scalable, systematic method for finding all faults in neuromorphic chips using only a linear number of tests, without requiring special design-for-testability features.
contributions: Algorithmic test generation for neuromorphic chips using fault activation and propagation mechanisms without DfT
O(L) complexity approach achieving 100% fault coverage scaling linearly with network depth
Test methodology robust to 4-bit weight quantization and 10% weight variation with zero test escape and overkill
73,000x reduction in total test length compared to previous work

metrics.other: 100% fault coverage, 73000x reduction in test length, robust to 4-bit quantization and 10% weight variation

primary_theme: Efficient test generation for neuromorphic hardware
